$comment: Riftlight authored opening draft. Development preview only; see ../README.md. Production campaign id will be riftlight. No bonus XP: preserve the design bible campaign budget.
title: The River Takes Another Valley

plate.narration: Two valleys run between the glacier ridges. An old path follows one; fresh water fills the other. High on the slope, a chipped stone marker still points along the ridge.

goal.text: Follow the changed river and find a safe way across.

steps.label: Get across to the far path

arrival.narration: Pip Thistledown, a young manticore scout, follows the road north with your party. Beyond the last stone keepers, the ground rises toward the glacier. Meltwater sounds where his sketch shows a dry valley. The familiar path ahead is cut in two. A yeti on the near bank holds up a walking staff, asking you to stop on the high ground before coming closer. Pip shuts his notebook. "We should look before we trust the old line."

variants.text: Your party chose to lead Pip's traveling page with the road plan. He keeps it open to compare with this changed route.
Pip keeps the uncertain stone count on his traveling page and opens a fresh space for what the valley shows now.

look_again.narration: Pip stops beside an old route marker, a dark stone with a fork-shaped chip. The path below it used to reach a narrow melt channel. Today that place is dry, and water is pouring between two ridges farther west. A yeti route worker waits on a broad shelf above the new flow. A bundle of tools lies on the opposite bank. Before anyone heads toward the worker, your party needs to tell a changed landmark from a changed river. What will you compare first?

choices.label: Compare the marker with both ridges
Trace the dry channel from firm ground

look_again_1.narration: You keep your feet on the upper path while Pip holds his drawing against the horizon. One friend checks the chipped marker; another points out the ridges. You look for the same shapes in the same order before putting a name on the water below.

look_again_1_check.prompt: Compare the marker with both ridges. Choose who leads while the others help.

look_again_1_done.narration: The marker and ridges still agree with the drawing. The water has taken another valley between them. Pip puts his finger on the blank space west of the old channel. You have a changed route to investigate, rather than a reason to throw away every familiar landmark.

look_again_1_changed.narration: A curl of snow hides one ridge and your first comparison points the wrong way. You wait for the gust to pass and compare the chipped marker again. The correction leaves the same conclusion: the landmarks agree, but the water between them has changed its course.

look_again_2.narration: You follow the visible bed only along its firm upper edge. Pip watches where it joins the valley ahead. Your party marks the last place water has recently passed without stepping into the new stream or assuming the dry stones will stay dry.

look_again_2_check.prompt: Trace the dry channel from firm ground. Choose who leads while the others help.

look_again_2_done.narration: The marker and ridges still agree with the drawing. The water has taken another valley between them. Pip puts his finger on the blank space west of the old channel. You have a changed route to investigate, rather than a reason to throw away every familiar landmark.

look_again_2_changed.narration: A curl of snow hides one ridge and your first comparison points the wrong way. You wait for the gust to pass and compare the chipped marker again. The correction leaves the same conclusion: the landmarks agree, but the water between them has changed its course.

worker_signal.narration: The yeti worker raises a walking staff and points at the broad shelf beside them. A dark wet seam crosses the short route to it. The worker does not wave you forward. Pip starts to call a question, then remembers how sound carries over the ice. You can reach the shelf by a longer rock path or ask the worker to point out a waiting place from where you stand. Neither requires a jump over the seam. How will you approach?

choices.label: Take the longer rock path at the worker's pace
Use quiet hand signals to agree where to wait

worker_signal_1.narration: You point to the rock path and wait for the worker to nod before moving. Pip stays with the slowest friend. At each turn you check that the next foothold is rock rather than snow over a gap. The worker has time to put the staff down and meet you.

worker_signal_2.narration: You hold up an open hand and point to the broadest ground near your party. The worker points to its upper edge, then takes the rock path toward you. Nobody has to make the doubtful seam into a shortcut merely to begin a conversation.

two_jobs.narration: The worker introduces herself as one of the yetis who checks paths between the glacier reading rooms. Her packed food and spare rope are already on this bank. Across the new stream, a tool bundle rests beside an unlit trail lantern. Both can be recovered later, but the lantern marks a path other visitors may still follow. A second worker is due along that path. She asks your party which warning should be dealt with first. What is the immediate danger?

choices.label: Make the old approach stop before the new water
Signal the far approach from the broad shelf

two_jobs_1.narration: You ask Pip to carry a clear stop signal back to the last safe turn while the party remains with the worker. She lends him a strip of dark cloth from her pack. Visitors can stop on firm ground before they try to reach a lantern on the wrong bank.

two_jobs_2.narration: You help the worker lift her staff where it is visible above the flow. A friend keeps watch on the old path while Pip compares the lantern's position with the ridge. If someone appears across the stream, you can show the waiting place before asking them to cross.

test_flow.narration: The worker places three loose stones on a board to stand for the two banks and a central rock. She has not checked that rock since the water arrived. Mist keeps hiding its low side. Your party can measure the flow past it or look along the bank for a wider, shallower reach. A fast answer would help the coming visitor, but a guessed crossing would put them in the stream. Which test will give you something you can use?

choices.label: Time floating twigs past the central rock
Survey the wider reach from two dry viewpoints

test_flow_1.narration: You collect loose twigs from the worker's pack and drop them from firm ground. Two friends watch separate points while Pip follows the path downstream. You do not reach into the flow to rescue a twig. The worker counts only trials everyone could see.

test_flow_1_check.prompt: Time floating twigs past the central rock. Choose who leads while the others help.

test_flow_1_done.narration: The tests show a short calm pocket behind the central rock and a rougher run beyond it. You mark the pocket as a place for a rope to rest, not a place for a hero to stand. The wider reach has a firm approach for an alternative route.

test_flow_1_changed.narration: Spray hides the result halfway through. You refuse to call the missing part safe. The worker shows you a higher viewpoint where the bank is firm, and you make a smaller plan from what can be seen there. The uncertain central rock stays off the walking route.

test_flow_2.narration: You stay on the bank and compare the exposed stones from above and below. Pip marks where spray hides the bed. Your party asks the worker which parts were checked before the change, keeping those older checks separate from anything you can verify now.

test_flow_2_check.prompt: Survey the wider reach from two dry viewpoints. Choose who leads while the others help.

test_flow_2_done.narration: The tests show a short calm pocket behind the central rock and a rougher run beyond it. You mark the pocket as a place for a rope to rest, not a place for a hero to stand. The wider reach has a firm approach for an alternative route.

test_flow_2_changed.narration: Spray hides the result halfway through. You refuse to call the missing part safe. The worker shows you a higher viewpoint where the bank is firm, and you make a smaller plan from what can be seen there. The uncertain central rock stays off the walking route.

bundle_plan.narration: The second worker arrives on the far path and stops beside the lantern. She can see your signal and has room to wait. The tool bundle is beside her, but she has no spare line long enough for the stream. Your worker offers two coils of rope from her pack and a broad carrying board. Your party can prepare to move the tools first or leave them with the far worker while securing a route for people. What will help the two workers most?

choices.label: Prepare a line for the tool bundle first
Secure a waiting and crossing plan before moving tools

bundle_plan_1.narration: You ask the far worker to keep the bundle well back from the water until the line is ready. The near worker coils the loose end on firm ground. Pip helps your party check that pulling the tools cannot pull a waiting hero toward the bank.

bundle_plan_2.narration: You leave the bundle with the far worker and mark where people should stand on both sides. Your worker agrees to keep her food and second rope ready as backup. The tools can wait while everyone learns which signal means stop and which means proceed.

anchor.narration: A firm rock projects from the upper bank beside the worker. It could hold the near end of a guide rope, but thin ice hides its base. Farther back, two sound rocks give a longer line with less convenient reach. The worker asks your party to choose where it can safely take weight. A thornguard can help steady the carrying board, but no ability will make an unchecked anchor sound. Which support will you test?

choices.label: Clear a small view of the projecting rock's base
Use the two higher rocks with a longer guide line
Use brace to steady the carrying board

anchor_1.narration: You work from the firm side and lift only loose surface snow with the board's edge. A friend holds the spare line away from the stream. The worker watches for movement at the base, ready to stop before the anchor is asked to hold anybody.

anchor_1_check.prompt: Clear a small view of the projecting rock's base. Choose who leads while the others help.

anchor_1_done.narration: The support stays steady under the careful test. You stop adding weight once the worker can judge the line. She marks the tested arrangement on Pip's drawing and keeps the spare rope free. Nobody treats a successful test as permission to rush the crossing.

anchor_1_changed.narration: The first arrangement shifts under the board. You stop before anyone puts weight on it. The worker moves the support back onto the rock path and helps your party rebuild the turn. The shorter reach is abandoned; the longer line has a clear, checked route.

anchor_2.narration: You take the rope back to the rock path and lay out a wide turn between the two supports. Pip keeps the spare coil clear of your feet. Your party tests the arrangement with the board first so a catch can be noticed without anyone being on the line.

anchor_2_check.prompt: Use the two higher rocks with a longer guide line. Choose who leads while the others help.

anchor_2_done.narration: The support stays steady under the careful test. You stop adding weight once the worker can judge the line. She marks the tested arrangement on Pip's drawing and keeps the spare rope free. Nobody treats a successful test as permission to rush the crossing.

anchor_2_changed.narration: The first arrangement shifts under the board. You stop before anyone puts weight on it. The worker moves the support back onto the rock path and helps your party rebuild the turn. The shorter reach is abandoned; the longer line has a clear, checked route.

signals.narration: The far worker lifts the lantern to ask whether she should move. Your worker shakes her head and looks to your party. Spray can hide a spoken instruction, and both workers have tools to carry. Pip suggests three simple signals, but a sign that means start to one person might mean stop to another. You can rehearse while everyone is still on firm ground. How will the far worker show that she understood rather than merely saw you?

choices.label: Have each bank repeat the signal before anyone moves
Make stopping the one signal anyone can give

signals_1.narration: You show stop, wait and proceed one at a time. The far worker repeats each with the lantern before putting it back on the rock. Pip watches both banks and corrects a mixed-up gesture during the rehearsal. The rope stays slack until everyone agrees.

signals_2.narration: You agree on a broad stop signal and let the workers choose one clear invitation to proceed. A friend practices interrupting the invitation from the near bank. Both workers stop at once. A small doubt can now halt the plan without needing a louder voice.

tools_return.narration: With the signals understood, the far worker ties the tool bundle to the end of the carrying line. It is not tied to her body. Your party must guide the bundle over the water without letting its loose straps catch. One worker watches the far edge and the other stands beside the near anchor. You can keep the bundle low along the guide rope or use the broad board to hold its straps together. Which method will you try?

choices.label: Guide the bundle steadily along the rope
Make a broad sling with the carrying board
Have a duskrunner secure the loose straps

tools_return_1.narration: You ask the far worker to tuck in every strap before the pull begins. One friend pulls from firm ground while another keeps the returning coil out of the stream. Pip watches the central rock and gives the stop signal as soon as the bundle approaches a snag.

tools_return_1_check.prompt: Guide the bundle steadily along the rope. Choose who leads while the others help.

tools_return_1_done.narration: The bundle reaches the near bank with every tool still packed. You set it well above the wet seam and untie the hauling line. The far worker now has free hands for the crossing, and the guide rope can be checked without a load hanging from it.

tools_return_1_changed.narration: A strap catches before the bundle is halfway across. You give the stop signal and take the strain off the line. The far worker draws it back to firm ground, repacks the strap and passes the tools by the higher rock reach with your worker guiding. Nothing is left dangling.

tools_return_2.narration: You fasten the bundle against the board and leave its handles visible. The workers check the knot from their own sides. Your party can bring the whole shape across without guessing where a loose tool ends. The spare rope remains available if the board catches.

tools_return_2_check.prompt: Make a broad sling with the carrying board. Choose who leads while the others help.

tools_return_2_done.narration: The bundle reaches the near bank with every tool still packed. You set it well above the wet seam and untie the hauling line. The far worker now has free hands for the crossing, and the guide rope can be checked without a load hanging from it.

tools_return_2_changed.narration: A strap catches before the bundle is halfway across. You give the stop signal and take the strain off the line. The far worker draws it back to firm ground, repacks the strap and passes the tools by the higher rock reach with your worker guiding. Nothing is left dangling.

crossing_choice.narration: The worker shows you two ways to reach the far path and the reading rooms beyond it. The prepared rope line gives a short supported crossing along a low shelf. The higher rock reach takes longer and needs careful footing, but avoids the low ice. Both are checked routes with a spare plan if conditions change. Pip asks which one the party wants to attempt together. You will not split the group or leave a friend to manage alone. Which way will you take?

choices.label: Cross together using the supported low shelf
Take the longer route over the high rock reach

crossing_choice_1.narration: You leave the tools on firm ground and check the guide line before the first hero moves. The workers agree who will watch each bank. Pip waits until every friend knows where to stop. If the low shelf shifts, the higher rock reach remains the way to finish.

crossing_choice_1_check.prompt: Cross together using the supported low shelf. Choose who leads while the others help.

crossing_choice_1_done.narration: The chosen route holds and the party reaches the far path together. The workers wait until the last friend is on firm ground before lifting the stop signal. Pip checks every face, then gives the all-clear. Your crossing plan has worked without leaving anyone behind. You finish along the supported low shelf.

crossing_choice_1_changed.narration: The first step shows a change in the chosen route. Everyone stops at the agreed place while the workers keep the backup ready. Your party returns to firm ground, then crosses by the other checked route together. A changed plan gets everyone across; nobody has to win a second roll. You finish by the high rock reach.

crossing_choice_2.narration: You coil the hauling line and leave the guide rope ready as backup. The worker points out the footholds she has checked. Your party moves at the slowest friend's pace, with Pip keeping the group together. No one is asked to jump across an unseen gap.

crossing_choice_2_check.prompt: Take the longer route over the high rock reach. Choose who leads while the others help.

crossing_choice_2_done.narration: The chosen route holds and the party reaches the far path together. The workers wait until the last friend is on firm ground before lifting the stop signal. Pip checks every face, then gives the all-clear. Your crossing plan has worked without leaving anyone behind. You finish by the high rock reach.

crossing_choice_2_changed.narration: The first step shows a change in the chosen route. Everyone stops at the agreed place while the workers keep the backup ready. Your party returns to firm ground, then crosses by the other checked route together. A changed plan gets everyone across; nobody has to win a second roll. You finish along the supported low shelf.

river_turn.narration: From the far path, the ridges look familiar but the stream points down the valley your earlier map left dry. Pip asks whether he should erase the old watercourse. The workers refuse to promise that the new flow will last. A wet seam is already growing near the old channel. Your party has seen a change, not a permanent new map of the realm. How should the drawing preserve both the old route and what happened today?

choices.label: Keep the old channel and add the observed new course
Make a separate crossing sketch instead of erasing the map

river_turn_1.narration: You give each course its own line and mark the place where your party stood. Pip writes that the new line was observed during this crossing. The workers can compare another visit without mistaking today's record for a promise that the water will always run here.

river_turn_2.narration: You keep the earlier map intact and draw a second page with the ridges, guide line and high reach. Pip puts both pages together. Anyone using them will have to look at the valley again, just as your party did, before choosing a crossing.

return_water.narration: A narrow tongue of water begins creeping along the old bed behind you. The stream in the western valley falls quieter. The workers stop moving the tools and ask everyone to stay on the upper path. There is time to lift the guide rope and lantern from their low positions, but not to make a wall across either channel. Your party can help the workers withdraw the equipment without pretending to direct where the river goes. What should come up first?

choices.label: Lift the low guide rope before the old bed fills
Move the lantern and waiting marker to the upper path

return_water_1.narration: You keep all the heroes on firm ground and pull the loose rope back from above. One worker watches the rising tongue of water while Pip keeps the coil from spreading across the path. The far worker stands ready to leave the lantern if its footing changes.

return_water_1_check.prompt: Lift the low guide rope before the old bed fills. Choose who leads while the others help.

return_water_1_done.narration: The equipment reaches the upper path before the water covers the low shelf. You leave both channels clear. The workers look from one valley to the other while Pip marks the change in order. Your party has helped people adapt without claiming to have turned the river back.

return_water_1_changed.narration: Water reaches one low marker before it can be lifted. Your party leaves it and withdraws to the upper path. The workers keep the useful rope and lantern, then place a fresh warning higher up. Pip records the abandoned marker so nobody follows it as an invitation.

return_water_2.narration: You help the far worker carry the lantern clear of the returning water and set it beside a broad stopping place. Pip keeps watch on the low rope while the other worker draws it in. The new warning will point to firm ground whichever channel fills next.

return_water_2_check.prompt: Move the lantern and waiting marker to the upper path. Choose who leads while the others help.

return_water_2_done.narration: The equipment reaches the upper path before the water covers the low shelf. You leave both channels clear. The workers look from one valley to the other while Pip marks the change in order. Your party has helped people adapt without claiming to have turned the river back.

return_water_2_changed.narration: Water reaches one low marker before it can be lifted. Your party leaves it and withdraws to the upper path. The workers keep the useful rope and lantern, then place a fresh warning higher up. Pip records the abandoned marker so nobody follows it as an invitation.

tell_together.narration: The water now runs again along the older bed. The western course still glistens between the ridges, showing where it briefly passed. Your worker asks each witness for the sequence before the two workers compare their own accounts. A strong voice could easily make everyone copy its version. Pip offers to write, but he waits for your plan. How can the group preserve differences that might matter to the reading-room keepers?

choices.label: Let each bank describe the change before comparing notes
Have one friend draw while another points to landmarks

tell_together_1.narration: You ask the near and far workers for their own order of signals, crossing and returning water. Your party speaks last, from the path you actually took. Pip marks where the views agree and where spray hid a moment. Nobody fills that gap with a guess.

tell_together_2.narration: You rebuild the sequence on the page from the marker and ridges rather than from whoever speaks fastest. The workers point out the moments they could not see. Pip leaves those parts dotted. The complete group can agree on a change without claiming one perfect view.

next_witness.narration: The worker offers to take your account to an elder yeti at a nearby reading room. A newly exposed piece of memory ice has also shown a river leaving by another valley, but she will not explain what she has not read herself. You can ask to see it with her or send the account ahead while making your own careful approach. Both routes follow the upper path you have checked. What should the elder receive first?

choices.label: Bring the crossing witnesses and their separate accounts
Send a clear sketch ahead with the returning worker

next_witness_1.narration: You ask both workers whether they want to come. One will carry the tools onward; the other agrees to walk with your party. Pip keeps both accounts visible. The elder will be able to ask which view belongs to which bank instead of receiving one voice pretending to be everyone.

next_witness_2.narration: You give the worker a copy showing the ridges and sequence, with the uncertain moments left dotted. Your party keeps the original and follows the upper path. Pip notes who carried the copy so a later disagreement can begin by checking the pages rather than blaming a messenger.

last_check.narration: Before leaving the crossing, the workers ask your party to test the upper warning as if you had just arrived. The river looks ordinary again from one direction. The abandoned low approach could tempt a traveler who never saw it change. Pip plays that traveler while you stand beside the new lantern. Your work is only useful if it still makes sense when the strange moment has passed. Which instruction should he be able to repeat in his own words?

choices.label: Repeat where to stop and which ground was checked
Repeat what must be looked at again on the next visit

last_check_1.narration: You let Pip approach without hints until he reaches the new warning. He points out the upper waiting place and both former crossing options. Your party corrects any instruction that sounds like a permanent guarantee. The workers keep the version he can actually follow.

last_check_1_check.prompt: Repeat where to stop and which ground was checked. Choose who leads while the others help.

last_check_1_done.narration: Pip stops well above the low bed and explains what changed without claiming the party caused it. The workers take over the warning. They can maintain a useful route after your party leaves, and you can carry the witnessed change toward the reading room.

last_check_1_changed.narration: Pip follows one part of the old approach before the warning makes sense. You halt the rehearsal and shift the lantern into view. On the next walk he stops on the upper path. The workers thank you for correcting the warning while correction is easy.

last_check_2.narration: You ask Pip to identify the marker, both ridges and the two channel beds. He compares the view with your drawing before offering a route. The workers add one short reminder to the lantern: stop on the upper path and look before following yesterday's water.

last_check_2_check.prompt: Repeat what must be looked at again on the next visit. Choose who leads while the others help.

last_check_2_done.narration: Pip stops well above the low bed and explains what changed without claiming the party caused it. The workers take over the warning. They can maintain a useful route after your party leaves, and you can carry the witnessed change toward the reading room.

last_check_2_changed.narration: Pip follows one part of the old approach before the warning makes sense. You halt the rehearsal and shift the lantern into view. On the next walk he stops on the upper path. The workers thank you for correcting the warning while correction is easy.

rest.narration: The workers keep the lantern on the upper path. Your party has crossed, and the river has returned to its older bed after briefly running down the other valley. Pip carries the sequence rather than an explanation for its cause. The yeti worker points to the reading-room path. "An elder is looking at a memory. We should compare what was seen." You can continue toward the memory ice or return by the upper road.

anchor_assisted.narration: A thornguard steadies the carrying board with brace while your party tests the anchor from firm ground. The worker watches the rock, not the strongest hero's confidence. Whoever can best judge the load may lead the check; the ability supplies support without making uncertain ice sound.

anchor_assisted_check.prompt: Use brace to steady the carrying board. The qualified hero assists; choose who leads the team check.

tools_return_assisted.narration: A duskrunner works from the safe bank to secure the bundle's loose straps before the haul. The workers hold their signals while your party prepares the line. The most nimble friend can lead the pull; nobody has to stand on the doubtful central rock.

tools_return_assisted_check.prompt: Have a duskrunner secure the loose straps. The qualified hero assists; choose who leads the team check.

voiceGuide.tone: Warm, funny, curious, with real consequences. Describe actions and sensory details directly. Short dialogue. Never use "the kind of thing that", "the sort of thing that", or "it was X, the type of thing that makes you Y" comparisons. Let a character act instead of explaining how the reader should feel.
voiceGuide.vocabulary: Read aloud to an eight-year-old. Concrete words, short sentences, distinct voices.

npcVoices.Pip Thistledown: Manticore scout. Eager but learns to separate observation from guess; never knows an unseen event.
npcVoices.Yeti keepers: Slow, enormous and gentle. Deliberate before answering. Offer a safe method and leave unknown history unknown.
